author: Declaration Desk
title: Bengal to hire 7,190 for rural jobs scheme as Adhikari reviews slow start with BDOs
dek: After a review with block officials, the chief minister said the state had generated 65.62 lakh person-days under the 125-day scheme and claimed 31 lakh fake job cards from the previous government's time had been found.
body:
West Bengal will recruit 7,190 people to the Panchayat Affairs and Rural Development Department to speed up work under the new 125-day rural employment scheme, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday after a review meeting with block development officers (BDOs) at the department's headquarters in Salt Lake. The West Bengal Public Service Commission will run the recruitment, which is to be completed by April 2027 under new rules meant to make the process transparent, he said, according to an IANS report.

Adhikari said the state had so far generated 65.62 lakh person-days of work under the scheme, that about 22 lakh people were being given work every day, and that around 10 lakh new job cards had been issued. "We are confident of meeting the target set by the Union government," he said. The state has not published block-wise figures, and the numbers are the chief minister's own; The Declaration could not check them against the scheme's dashboard.

## What the chief minister said

Adhikari also said about 31 lakh fake job-card holders dating from the previous Trinamool Congress government had been identified when job cards were linked with Aadhaar, and that some of them had received payments, IANS reported. He gave no breakdown or evidence for the figure. The Trinamool Congress had not responded by the time this report was filed.

He said more than Rs 13,000 crore had been earmarked for the scheme in the state, with the Centre contributing about Rs 8,000 crore and the state about Rs 5,000 crore, and that the Centre had released Rs 1,200 crore in the first phase. Panchayat Minister Dilip Ghosh, Minister of State Santanu Pramanik and Agriculture Minister Dudhkumar Mondal attended the meeting.

Before the meeting, Adhikari had said at a review with senior secretaries last week that BDOs who were not giving the scheme enough importance could be transferred, Millennium Post reported. No transfers were announced on Wednesday.

## Where Bengal stands

Bartaman reported on 1 November that Bengal was at the bottom of the national table, with about 50 lakh person-days generated this financial year against a target of 30 crore. Wednesday's figure of 65.62 lakh suggests some progress since, but it is still a small fraction of that target with five months of the financial year left. The two figures may not be measured on the same basis, and neither has been published by the state.

## What the scheme is

The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), known as VB-G RAM G, replaced the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). Parliament passed it in December 2025, according to PRS Legislative Research. It raises the annual guarantee of wage work for a rural household from 100 to 125 days.

Unlike MGNREGA, under which the Centre paid the full wage bill, the new scheme is shared 60:40 between the Centre and most states, with the Centre setting a normative allocation for each state and states bearing any spending above it. States must also announce in advance a pause of up to 60 days a year during peak sowing and harvesting, when no work is offered.

Bengal launched the scheme on 1 July 2026, covering about 2.56 crore job-card holders, The News Mill reported, citing ANI. The Centre approved a contribution of Rs 8,508 crore and the state allocated Rs 5,672 crore. Wages are paid directly into workers' accounts, and work must be provided within 15 days of a demand or an unemployment allowance becomes payable.

## Background

Rural job work in Bengal had already shrunk sharply before the switch. Central funds for MGNREGA in the state were stopped from March 2022 after the Centre cited irregularities, a dispute that ran for years between the previous Trinamool Congress government and the Union government.

Nationally, the new scheme had a slow start. Official dashboard data showed 7.67 crore person-days in July 2026, its first month, about half the 15.33 crore recorded in July 2025, Outlook reported in August. The Ministry of Rural Development disputed that, saying around 9 crore person-days had been generated during the transition month, and pointed to a budget estimate of Rs 95,692 crore for 2026-27.

## What happens next

- The WBPSC is to run the recruitment for 7,190 posts, to be completed by April 2027.
- The state has not said when it will publish block-wise progress figures.
- Because the Centre's share is capped at the state's normative allocation, how quickly Bengal can create work in the remaining months will also decide how much central money it draws this year.
